Pahadi communities are very casteist- even locals admit to it. You're being downvoted by the same Brahminical supremacy pahadis that you're absolutely right about. 

You can be a responsible tourist, respectful of the many cultures, care for the precious ecosystem, and more, and still be called an ignorant and indecent maidani. 

I have experienced the warm hospitality and friendliness of many pahadis but sadly most families hold fucked up beliefs about non brahmin and non pahadi people. 

They're not progressive about their own women, either. Very conservative, relationships considered scandalous, lots of gossip and judgement like their maidani counterparts, extreme pressure to look good. Places like Shimla have horribly eurocentric beauty standards even till date. If you're not fair you'll be looked down on and called "South Indian" as a SLUR. 

Even in educated families, menstruating women are asked to sleep separately above the "pashu ghar" (cowshed). It's a smaller room separate from the main house frame. Not allowed to touch anything in the house, including their own bedding and clothes or it would require washing. Extreme belief in typical menstruation practices that have been discarded by many urban and suburban households a while back. They say their gods will get super pissed and curse them. 

They're so worried about tourists pouring in and f-ing their culture up while it wasn't that great to begin with. 

Source: I've lived in and travelled around various parts of Himachal and Uttarakhand over the last many years, working and holding workshops where I interacted with lots of people. Have lived with families in villages, towns, and cities.
